title: Informal Conjecture (diameter bound improvement)
statement_text: The extra factor $\sqrt{\log n}$ (compared with the random tree $T_n$) in the diameter bound $5\sqrt{n \log n}$ for the block tree $BT(R_n)$ could be replaced by any function tending to $\infty$.
context_text: A block of a graph is a maximal 2-connected subgraph, or a bridge, or an isolated vertex. A class of graphs (closed under isomorphism) is block-stable if a graph belongs to it if and only if each of its blocks does (e.g. forests, any minor-closed class with 2-connected excluded minors, graphs whose blocks are triangles); more generally it is weakly block-stable if it is closed under replacing a graph by any graph with the same vertex set whose components have the same numbers of blocks of each isomorphism type. The block tree $BT(G)$ of a connected graph $G$ is the bipartite graph with a node $x_v$ for each vertex $v$ and a node $y_B$ for each block $B$, $x_v$ and $y_B$ being adjacent if and only if $v\in B$; the block forest $BF(G)$ is the disjoint union of the block trees of the components. $R_n$ is a uniformly random graph on vertex set $\{1,\dots,n\}$ from the class, and whp means with probability tending to $1$. The authors prove that for every weakly block-stable class, whp $BF(R_n)$ has diameter at most $5\sqrt{n\log n}$ (and in particular this holds for the block tree of a random connected graph from a block-stable class). A uniformly random labelled tree $T_n$ has diameter of order $\sqrt n$ with probability close to $1$, so the bound is off by a factor $\sqrt{\log n}$; the conjecture is presumably that, for any function $\omega(n)\to\infty$, the diameter should be whp at most $\omega(n)\sqrt n$.
notes: Stated in prose immediately before Theorem 1.2: 'We conjecture that the extra factor √log n (compared with the random tree Tn) could be replaced by any function tending to ∞.' No labelled conjecture environment.
paper_title: Random graphs from a block-stable class
